  note = {\textbf{Absorbs EDN-70 and EDN-78} (2026-10-05, 2026-10-06): the tree ceiling, and the search over both LightGBM variants.},

  decision = {\texttt{learning\_\allowbreak{}rate} 0.05 and \texttt{num\_\allowbreak{}leaves} 63 stay, because no search found a point measurably better on the validation split.
A committed hyperparameter is replaced only under the protocol in the pipeline docs: selection on the validation split alone, by L1, and only when the simultaneous 95\,\% interval of the difference lies below zero.
\texttt{n\_\allowbreak{}estimators} is a ceiling of 5,000 with early stopping after 50 rounds.
\texttt{tune.\allowbreak{}py} runs a search outside \texttt{dvc repro} and keeps its record in MLflow only.
NFR-10's 15 minutes cover the final fit; a search's energy is reported apart.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item Adopt the point with the lowest validation L1: its gain lies inside the noise.
\item Random or Optuna search with cross-validation: a new dependency and about five times the fits, for a region found flat.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} Across the twelve points of the first grid, no interval of the difference to the committed point lies below zero.
At 1,000 the ceiling ended both fits; at 5,000 the validation curve decides the tree count.
The search of 2026-10-06 covered both LightGBM variants and \texttt{min\_\allowbreak{}child\_\allowbreak{}samples}, reproduced the first grid, and kept every committed value.},

For the search of 2026-10-06 AI recommended committing the sweep records beside MLflow; Kevin had it check the course demo, which keeps its emissions in MLflow only, and chose that.},
